Subject: Re: Residency / APAC failover - internal technical options

Chloe / Ben / Laura — internal technical note.

Options we should present (brief):

A) EU primary + APAC cold metadata-only standby (default, lower cost, fastest legal alignment)
   - Only identifiers and routing metadata replicated to APAC (encrypted). No inference logs or PII at rest in APAC.
   - KMS: EU keys only. APAC nodes accept encrypted tokens but cannot decrypt without explicit key material export (manual step).
   - Failover: manual authorization required (customer sign-off + runbook). RTO target: 2-4 hours depending on cache warmup.

B) EU primary + APAC warm-passive standby (recommended for low RTO)
   - Selective replication: anonymized inference cache + non-PII operational logs; PII remains encrypted under customer CMK (split key policy).
   - KMS: Customer-managed keys in EU. Optionally configure CMK in APAC (customer-provided) for DR-only decryption; requires legal sign-off for key escrow/replication policy.
   - Failover: automated with approval gate (API token + audit trail). RTO: <30 mins typical.

C) Full geo-replication (not recommended unless contractually approved)
   - Replicates all datasets to APAC, full key replication required, significant legal and risk review.

Action items for decision doc:
- State default = Option A.
- If customer wants B/C, we need written sign-off, KMS config form, and updated SLA notes.

Attachments: WAN peering checklist and KMS notes for legal. Also note we need to run a DR tabletop with compliance present.

-Karthik
Senior Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Paul — attaching the formal Decision Record we discussed and a short diff of the runbook (high level). Summary below.

Residency Decision Record (summary):
- Primary region: EU (Frankfurt) — all PII and inference logs kept in EU by default.
- APAC role: Hot-passive standby that holds only encrypted routing metadata and non-PII operational metrics. No PII at rest in APAC unless customer explicitly configures Option B.
- KMS policy: Customer-managed CMK in EU for all PII. APAC keys are optional and require a separate KMS replication approval. No automatic export of EU CMK to APAC without written authorization.
- Failover model: Default = manual-authorized failover (trigger via authorized API + approval email + runbook). Option B (warm-passive automatic with approval gate) available upon signed addendum.
- Testing: Quarterly DR tests; Redwood will provide test logs and evidence (audit trail) after each exercise.

Attached: residency-decision-record-20280607.pdf (formalized) and runbook-diff.txt (high level callouts).

Next steps we propose:
1) You confirm acceptance of default Option A in writing (reply OK).
2) Schedule a 60m DR tabletop involving your compliance + our infra team (suggested dates listed in the attachment).
3) If Option B is required, sign the KMS/replication addendum and we will provide a KMS onboarding checklist.

We can join your procurement packet with the attached PDF as the decision record.

Best,
Chloe
